Subject: Term questions — operator license swap and billing clawback

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency/throughput benchmarks. Procurement asked me to get a bit more color on two commercial levers before we route to legal:

1) Operator licenses vs platform fee: we prefer to treat the "operator" licenses as an optional add-on (we’ll run a small on-prem pilot with our infra team). That means we may want to swap some platform fee into per-operator licenses after year 1. How flexible is Redwood on a mid-term swap?

2) Clawback / underutilization credits: we need an explicit mechanism so we’re not locked into full platform-fee amortization if consumption is materially below committed levels in year 1. Ideally something that returns a portion of unused committed value after Q2 and Q4 reconciliations.

Other asks: can you show a sample billing cadence (invoice timing + SOW milestones) and a draft of the clause that governs burst capacity (we may need to exceed reserved GPU pool for specific experiments)?

I attached our standard procurement worksheet — it has the internal timelines.

Thanks,
Elisa Gomez
VP, Cloud Platform
Zephyr Health

Subject: Re: Term questions — operator license swap and billing clawback

Elisa — thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers and a couple of concrete options below. Attaching an edited term sheet and a draft billing workback.

Short answers:
- Swap flexibility: yes, we can support a one-time mid-term swap of committed platform fee into operator licenses (subject to timing windows and a one-time admin fee). We typically allow swaps at the end of a quarter, with a 60-day notice.
- Clawback: we can offer a two-stage reconciliation: a soft reconciliation at 6 months (credit reserve) and a formal clawback at 12 months if utilization < 60% of committed baseline. The clawback would be capped at 30% of the unamortized platform fee.
- Burst rights: we provide an explicit burst entitlement with pre-agreed per-GPU spot pricing and a safety cap to protect other tenants; bursts are charged either as overage or purchased as temporary operator licenses depending on the option you pick.

Two packaging options for Zephyr to consider:
Option A — Lower platform fee + operator licenses on top
- Platform fee: amortized over 24 months, lower up-front (25% lower than Option B)
- Operator licenses: charged per-seat (annual), you start with 5 operator licenses for pilot and can add monthly pro-rations
- Swap: allowed once after month 12, admin fee 5% of swapped value
- Clawback: 12-month reconciliation, 20% cap on clawback

Option B — Higher platform fee, operator licenses included
- Platform fee: higher (covers fixed infra + support), amortized over 36 months
- Operator licenses: included up to 10 operators
- Swap: not applicable (already included)
- Clawback: 12-month reconciliation, 10% cap on clawback

Billing cadence proposal:
- Quarterly invoices for platform fee amortization (net 30)
- Monthly invoices for operator licenses and burst usage
- Reconciliation reports: monthly utilization metrics + formal Q2 and Q4 reconciliation statements

Next steps: Marissa, can you confirm the support-tier mapping for Option A vs B (S1/S2/S3 definitions)? Naomi, please confirm the impact to ARR math and a quick pro-forma comparing total cost of ownership across years 1–3. Elisa, I’ll set up a 30-min call after you review the term sheet to walk procurement through the swap mechanics.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Deals, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ZEP-2026-term-sheet-v2.pdf (pdf), billing-workback.xlsx (spreadsheet)

- Preferred billing: platform fee deferred until go-live makes approvals easier for our finance team. Can Redwood accept platform-fee invoices starting at go-live (with a small prepay to reserve capacity)?
- For the swap admin fee, procurement would prefer a fixed admin fee cap rather than a percentage (example: $25k cap).
- For clawback, we need the exact metric definition for "utilization" (is it token throughput? vGPU-hours? or a blended metric?). Please include example calculations in the next doc.

We can do a short call with finance next week if you can provide the billing example and the util metrics.

Procurement Team

- Prepay: 10% of first-year platform fee to reserve capacity (credited against first invoice at go-live)
- Swap admin fee: changed to a fixed cap of $25,000 (instead of 5%)
- Utilization metric: we propose a blended utilization metric (0.6 * billed vGPU-hours / committed vGPU-hours + 0.4 * production token throughput / committed throughput). We will include a worked example in the updated billing-workback.

Marissa — please confirm the S1/S2/S3 support definitions we will reference for the term sheet.
